title: SpaceX lines up a $40 billion lease for AI chips
friendlyTitle: SpaceX has lined up a $40 billion lease for AI chips
summary: SpaceX has a binding commitment for roughly $40 billion in financing for AI chips and related data-center equipment, disclosed in a Monday regulatory filing and described by the company as the largest committed GPU financing. An Apollo-managed entity will buy the hardware and lease it to SpaceX for about five to five and a quarter years, starting as each batch arrives. SpaceX expects to close by year-end, with leases beginning in the first half of 2027. Apollo said the chips are Nvidia's coming Vera Rubin generation.
friendlySummary: SpaceX has a binding commitment for about $40 billion in financing for AI chips and related data-center equipment. The company disclosed it in a Monday filing and called it the largest committed GPU financing. An entity managed by Apollo will buy the hardware and lease it to SpaceX for about five to five and a quarter years, starting as each batch arrives. SpaceX expects to close by the end of the year, with leases starting in the first half of 2027. Apollo said the chips are Nvidia's coming Vera Rubin generation.
whyItMatters: This is a lease, not a purchase you can copy, and it is separate from the compute Anthropic says it may buy from SpaceX. The part that reaches a smaller user is the price of the models those chips will run. SpaceX chief financial officer Bret Johnsen said the lease covers a notable share of the funding for the company's growth plans, and that SpaceX is seeing payback periods of less than a year on its AI infrastructure. That payback figure is the company's, not an outside audit.
